prompt.context_jp: 深夜の校閲部には、机の明かりだけ___小さく灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 深夜の校閲部には、机の明かりだけ(___)小さく灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? Note the 'only X' focus.

feedback.correct_en: The phrase 'だけ' with an exhaustive/exclusive focus ('only the desk light') calls for が — it identifies what uniquely was glowing in the dark office.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a general topic rather than pointing out the one thing that was lit; を doesn't fit an intransitive verb like 灯る.

contrast_examples.jp: 机の明かりだけが灯っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Only the desk light was on.

contrast_examples.jp: 机の明かりは灯っていた。
contrast_examples.en: As for the desk light, it was on (but this feels like contrast against something else).

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩が悦子に声をかける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事のペース(___)人それぞれですから、気にしなくていいですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in Fujiiwa's advice?

feedback.correct_en: 仕事のペース is the topic being commented on — 'as for work pace, it depends on the person.' は marks this general statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly single out work pace as new information, when it's really being set up as the topic of a generalization.

contrast_examples.jp: 今 誰が担当か分からない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't know who's in charge right now (new info → が).

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚の初登場シーン。
prompt.prompt_jp: 書籍編集部の貝塚八郎(___)、赤字だらけのゲラを片手に大股でやってきたのである。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces this new character into the scene?

feedback.correct_en: 貝塚八郎 is introduced here as new information — someone bursting into the scene for the first time. が marks this presentational introduction.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply he's already a known topic, but the narrative is announcing his arrival.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が怒っている理由。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悦子が初めて手がけたその校閲(___)、担当編集者の逆鱗に触れたらしい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the subject of 触れた?

feedback.correct_en: The proofreading she did is being reported as the thing that (newly) angered the editor — it's the identified cause, taking が in this subordinate clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would promote it to topic status, but the narrative is reporting a new fact about it.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の一言が逆鱗に触れた。
contrast_examples.en: His single word angered him (new cause).

contrast_examples.jp: その校閲は丁寧だった。

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が自分の仕事を誇る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私(___)初めて校閲した、記念すべきゲラじゃない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the relative clause describing the galley?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying ゲラ ('the galley that I proofread'), the subject typically takes が. は is generally avoided in such embedded modifying clauses.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the relative clause — は tends to mark topics of main clauses, not subjects inside noun-modifying clauses.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が怒鳴る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誤字脱字なんか どうだっていい。誰(___)こんな余計な指摘出しをしろっつった？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in '誰___'?

feedback.correct_en: Question words like 誰 asking 'who did X?' demand が — they seek new identifying information.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical in this interrogative context; you can't topicalize an unknown person.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が時代設定を説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本郷先生の小説の時代設定(___)常に昭和なんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for stating a defining characteristic?

feedback.correct_en: The period setting is the topic being characterized — 'as for the setting, it's always Showa.' は fits this definitional/topical statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow focus as if answering 'what is Showa?' — it doesn't match a general characterization.

contrast_examples.jp: この小説の舞台は東京だ。
舞台が東京なのはこの作品だけだ。
contrast_examples.en: The one whose setting is Tokyo is only this work (contrastive focus).

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が貝塚に反論する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恥かくの(___)あんたじゃなくて、あんたが大事にしてる作家先生なんだから。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up the contrast 'not you, but the writer'?

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized 恥かくの is the topic being identified: 'the one who'll lose face is not you, but the writer.' This cleft-like identification uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the sentence feel like fresh exhaustive listing, but the structure here is X は A じゃなくて B (topic + contrastive identification).

contrast_examples.en: The one at fault is not me.

contrast_examples.jp: 困るのはあなたですよ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who'll be in trouble is you.

prompt.context_jp: 本郷大作の紹介。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本郷大作といえば、二十年来の大御所(___)ある。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this characterization?

feedback.correct_en: である is the written/formal copula — N+である='is N.' This is a definitional statement calling for the copula form.
feedback.incorrect_en: がある would mean 'there exists,' not 'is'; にある would mean 'located at.'

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は有名な作家である。

contrast_examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: レストランの個室の描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 個室の扉を開けると、シャンパンクーラーの氷を前に、白髪の紳士(___)悠然と葉巻をくゆらせていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits when discovering someone in a scene?

feedback.correct_en: The white-haired gentleman is newly discovered as the door opens — presentational/new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply he's already a known topic, but the scene is just revealing him.

contrast_examples.jp: 扉を開けると、男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: When I opened the door, a man was standing there.

contrast_examples.jp: その男はタバコを吸っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が悦子を紹介する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女(___)校閲を担当した河野です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in '(this is the person who...)'?

feedback.correct_en: '彼女が校閲を担当した' is a relative clause modifying 河野 — 'Kono, the one who handled the proofreading.' Relative-clause subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は doesn't typically appear in such embedded modifying clauses that identify someone.

contrast_examples.jp: これが私が書いた本です。
contrast_examples.en: This is the book I wrote.

prompt.context_jp: レストランでの会話の様子。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会話の主導権(___)完全に本郷と悦子のもとに移っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the topic of this narration?

feedback.correct_en: 会話の主導権 is the topic being commented on across this sentence — 'the lead in the conversation had moved to...' は frames this known element.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would feel like reporting a surprising new fact about who-did-what, but here the narrator is tracking a known thread.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が主導権を握っているの？

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が立田橋の違和感に気づく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 全部 実際の名前なのに、1つだけ違うの(___)あってさ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'there's just one that's different'?

feedback.correct_en: The 'one that's different' is newly introduced existence — 'there's one' uses ある with が. Also, だけ focus pairs naturally with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat it as a known topic, but she's just discovering/presenting this anomaly.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩が校閲の原則を述べる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 作家(___)「ママでいい」と指定しているなら、そのままでいいのです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this conditional clause?

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate なら conditional clause, the subject is marked with が to identify who did the specifying.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a conditional subordinate clause would sound off here; the focus is on identifying the actor whose instruction matters.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生が言うなら従います。
contrast_examples.en: If the teacher says so, I'll obey.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚の叱責の後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 言葉の重み(___)、ゆっくりと悦子の胸に沈んでいった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this narrative event?

feedback.correct_en: The weight of the words is being presented as the thing that sank into her — a fresh narrative event, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat it as an ongoing topic, but the narrator is reporting a single sinking action in the moment.

prompt.context_jp: 本郷が悦子を叱る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 君のしたこと(___)校閲ではない。他人のプライバシーを踏みにじる行為だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 'What you did' is the topic being judged — は fits 'as for what you did, it's not proofreading.' Classic topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly focus 'what you did' as new information, but here it's a known subject being characterized/judged.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたの意見は正しい。
誰の意見が正しいか決める。
contrast_examples.en: We'll decide whose opinion is correct (question focus).

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が本郷に注意する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生、見た目に___ないでください。信じられないぐらい下品で口の悪い女なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb warns 'don't be fooled by appearances'?

feedback.correct_en: 見た目に騙される ('to be fooled by appearances') is the set collocation here — Kaizuka is warning Hongo not to be deceived.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見られる and 信じられる don't form this idiom; they wouldn't convey 'don't be deceived by looks.'

contrast_examples.en: I was fooled by his lies.

prompt.context_jp: 本郷の名前の威光。
prompt.prompt_jp: その名を耳にしただけで、若手編集者なら誰しも___を伸ばす存在だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom 'to straighten one's ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 背筋を伸ばす ('to straighten one's spine/back') is the idiom for sitting up in attention or respect.
feedback.incorrect_en: 背中を伸ばす is a literal stretch, and 腰を伸ばす usually means straightening up from bending — neither carries the 'show respect/snap to attention' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生の前で背筋を伸ばす。
疲れたので腰を伸ばした。
contrast_examples.en: I was tired so I stretched my back.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が怒る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰がこんな余計な___出しをしろっつった？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits to mean an 'unnecessary note/comment'?

feedback.correct_en: 指摘出し is the in-house proofreading term for the notes/queries a proofreader raises. The chapter title is also 「余計な指摘」.
feedback.incorrect_en: 注意出し and 命令出し aren't standard terms for proofreading queries.

prompt.context_jp: 本郷が悦子をからかう。
prompt.prompt_jp: まったく冗談が___なぁ、君は。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits in the idiom 'you can't take a joke'?

feedback.correct_en: 冗談が通じない is the fixed expression for 'can't take a joke / a joke doesn't land.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 分からない and 聞こえない aren't the idiomatic collocation; they'd sound unnatural with 冗談.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子がどうしても気になる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茶を淹れに立った悦子の胸には、どうしても___引っかかりが残っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'she couldn't back down'?

feedback.correct_en: 引き下がる means 'to back down/withdraw.' The narrator says she couldn't let it go — a nagging doubt she couldn't abandon.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き返す means physically 'turn back,' and 引き止める means 'to hold back (someone else)' — neither matches 'unable to let the matter drop.'

contrast_examples.jp: ここで引き下がれない。

prompt.context_jp: 茸原が藤岩に頼み込む。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今回は例外ってことで、___もらえませんか。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'cut her some slack / overlook it'?

feedback.correct_en: 大目に見る means 'to overlook / be lenient about.' Takihara is asking Fujiiwa to be lenient this once.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を奪う means 'to captivate,' 目を覚ます means 'to wake up / come to one's senses' — neither fits a request for leniency.

contrast_examples.jp: 今回だけ大目に見てください。
contrast_examples.en: Please let it slide just this once.

contrast_examples.jp: 目を覚ましてください。

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が茸原のお説教にうんざり。
prompt.prompt_jp: ええ、もう耳に___です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'I'm sick of hearing it'?

feedback.correct_en: 耳にタコができる literally 'a callus forms on my ear' means 'I've heard it so many times I'm sick of it.' Fixed idiom with タコ.
feedback.incorrect_en: イカ and カニ don't appear in this idiom; only タコ works.

contrast_examples.jp: その話はもう耳にタコだ。
contrast_examples.en: I've heard that story a hundred times.
It hits close to home (different idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が下宿に戻る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大将たちに心配を___ないように、彼女はドアの前で何度か表情を整えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits '(so as not to) cause worry'?

feedback.correct_en: 心配をかける is the fixed collocation for 'to cause (someone) worry.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配をやる/つける are not natural collocations in this sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 親に心配をかけたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to worry my parents.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が藤岩に目標を語る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for Etsuko's determined outburst?

choices.text: 1日も早く認めてもらいたいんです。
1日も早くに認めてもらいたいんです。

feedback.correct_en: 1日も早く is an adverbial phrase meaning 'as soon as possible' and takes no に. The に version is unnatural.
feedback.incorrect_en: Adding に after 早く breaks the standard adverbial pattern; native speakers don't say 早くに in this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: I want to return as soon as possible.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が本郷のシャンパンの誘いを断ろうとする場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural in Kaizuka's polite refusal?

choices.text: 今日はお叱りを受けに来ただけですので。
今日はお叱りを受けに来たばかりですので。

feedback.correct_en: 〜に来ただけ ('only came to...') fits the humble refusal — framing their purpose narrowly. The source line uses this.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜に来たばかり means 'just arrived' (temporal), which doesn't convey 'we came only to...' and wouldn't justify declining a drink.

contrast_examples.jp: 話を聞きに来ただけです。
今 着いたばかりです。

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が夜道を上機嫌で歩く場面の地の文。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'washing away all the hardship'?

choices.text: これまでの苦労を一気に洗い流した気がした。
これまでの苦労を一気に流し洗った気がした。

feedback.correct_en: 洗い流す ('to wash away') is the established compound verb. The metaphor 'wash away hardship' uses it idiomatically.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流し洗う isn't a standard compound; it reverses and breaks the collocation.

prompt.context_jp: 本郷が悦子に怒りを告げる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for Hongo's cold dismissal?

choices.text: 君のしたことは校閲ではない。
君がしたのは校閲ではないです。

feedback.correct_en: 君のしたこと ('what you did') as a noun phrase is cleaner and more cutting for a stern pronouncement. The plain-form ではない matches his authoritative tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: Mixing plain-form content with ですます (〜ではないです) creates an awkward register clash in such a grave rebuke.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が「新人への洗礼だ」と言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the natural idiom?

choices.text: いわゆる洗礼ってやつだ。
いわば洗礼ってやつだ。

feedback.correct_en: いわゆる〜ってやつだ ('it's what they call ~') is the fixed casual pattern with 〜ってやつ. いわゆる means 'so-called.'
feedback.incorrect_en: いわば ('so to speak') doesn't combine naturally with ってやつだ; the set phrase pairs いわゆる with ってやつ.

contrast_examples.jp: いわゆる天才ってやつだ。
contrast_examples.en: He's what you'd call a genius.

contrast_examples.jp: いわば家族のようなものだ。
contrast_examples.en: It's like family, so to speak.
